findings.text: The `command:<name>` event used to be emitted on the command itself. It is now emitted only on the parent, and only when a parent exists. A listener such as `cmd.on('command:foo')` or `program.on('command:'+program.name())` never fires, which is a backward-compatibility break.

A command with no action handler now emits on the parent whenever the parent has a listener for its name. This skips the operands/`*`/`command:*` handling and the later help or unknown-command fallthrough. A subcommand with its own subcommands, such as `parent sub unknownarg`, silently does nothing instead of reporting the unknown command.

0.reason: The change moves the command:<name> event emission from the command itself to its parent (and only when a parent exists), so listeners attached directly to the command or to the program under its own name will no longer fire, which is a genuine backward-compatibility break distinct from the reference bug about unknown-option masking.
